name: Duplicate child ids
documentation: NEGATIVE fixture. Two sibling collapsed subprocesses each declare a child NODE with id "check". Every rule in rules.js walks one container at a time and sees nothing wrong, and the geometry never notices either because a collapsed subprocess draws no children -- but the emitted BPMN carries the same xsd:ID twice, which is document-wide unique by definition, so no tool loads the file correctly. NC06 is the code that names it, and it names it because the NET is wrong too: transitions are keyed t_<node.id>, so the second node overwrites the first and the net has one transition where the model has two nodes. Deliberately NOT also duplicating a flow id -- two edges sharing an id are translated FAITHFULLY (places are keyed p_<src>_<tgt>[#k] and placeOfEdge is keyed by edge object identity), so NC06 does not and must not fire on them; that half of the class is caught by the bpmn-moddle round-trip in validation.xmlWarnings, where a 'duplicate ID' warning is now unconditionally fatal on the CLI generate path (exit 1, no files written, --strict or not). This fixture never reaches that gate: its duplicate is a NODE id, so NC06 stops it one gate earlier. Kept under tests/fixtures/negative/ so net-check.test.js's directory-wide fence -- which scans the top level of tests/fixtures/ only and requires every fixture there to be a clean translation -- is never asked to hold a fixture that exists to be dirty.
